text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak says what is going in Jerusalem now contradicts the Oslo agreement and permanent peace should be just. Mubarak gives important statements before leaving Rabat for home, saying that the Jerusalem Committee will hold a ministerial meeting in late March. Egypt offers help to the Palestinians and does not negotiate on their behalf, the president adds.
- A high Egyptian-Moroccsan committee, to be presided over by Mubarak and KingHassan, will meet every six months to coordinate in all fields.
- U.S. Vice President Al Gore's visit to Egypt in May aims at achieving progress in the relations between the two countries, a U.S. source tells al-Ahram.
- The Egyptian embassy in Tirana persuaded 60 Egyptian women and their children to be evacuated from Albania to Greek.
- The cabinet approves the first comprehensive bill on investment incentives. Projects in the South Valley will be offered a 20-year tax exemption.

- The fourth and last tunnel of the Peace Canal beneath the Suez Canal will be completed in May. The canal will carry 18 million cubic metres (635 million cubic feet) a day of Nile waters to north Sinai to irrigate about 400,000 acres (160,000 hectares).
- Mubarak issues a presidential ruling to regulate the Cairo and Alexandria stock exchanges.
